summary: async functions and await let several tasks take turns on one thread, and Promise.all waits for all of them. Because only one piece of code runs at a time, this.sold++ needs no lock.
notes: Each await pauses that booth and lets another booth run. Code between two awaits always runs without interruption.
booth() returns a Promise right away. Promise.all(booths) waits until every booth finishes and gives their results in the same order.
sellUnsafe() reads this.sold, awaits, then writes. All four booths read the same value before any writes, so the total is 100000 instead of 400000.
pitfall: Forgetting await before Promise.all(...) moves on before the booths finish, so the total prints as 0 with no error.
contrast: Python and Java threads can run at the same moment, so they need a Lock or synchronized. JavaScript runs your code on one thread and switches tasks only at await, so a counter is safe unless an await sits between reading and writing it.
